scope: Ranked the 13 records then marked priorRecognition=not-located by clarity of mismatch, importance of the affected safeguard, and potential reach. Read existing adverse-review notes, freshly checked selected primary sources and searched public coverage. No website content changed and no authority contacted.
discoveryLimit: No prior public identification of the exact selected discrepancies located in this bounded review. This cannot establish first discovery, absence of confidential Commission/government knowledge, or absence from unindexed/paywalled material.

ranking.conclusion: Strong apparent transposition defect in the legal status of interim occupational exposure limits. No workplace exceedance or injury established.
ranking.euRequirement: Directive 2024/869 Annex I inserts a binding diisocyanate table into Directive 98/24; interim eight-hour / short-term values are 10 / 20 micrograms NCO per cubic metre until 31 December 2028. Directive 98/24 Article 3(5) requires corresponding national binding limits. Transposition deadline 9 April 2026.
ranking.nationalVerification: Fresh live R4412-149, in force on 26 October 2026 and unchanged since 10 April, has 6 / 12 micrograms NCO per cubic metre applicable only from 1 January 2029. Order of 8 April 2026 expressly inserts 0.01 / 0.02 mg in the indicative table. R4412-150 calls indicative limits prevention objectives. R4412-28 requires immediate protection on exceedance of binding limits; R4412-29 requires risk reassessment for indicative exceedances. Annual accredited monitoring under R4412-27 continues for both.
ranking.significance: Affects the national response to exceeding limits for chemicals known to cause occupational asthma and sensitisation; not just a numerical or typographical discrepancy.
contraryChecks: General prevention and accredited monitoring remain mandatory.
REACH training restrictions are additional safeguards, not demonstrated replacement of a national binding interim ceiling.
No evidence that a particular exceedance is lawful, unaddressed, or caused injury.

novelty.outcome: No precise EU-versus-French legal-character criticism located.
knownCoverage: Présanse, 10 April 2026, describes indicative limits now and binding limits in 2029.
Prévention BTP, Réglementation Environnement, Tennaxia and other compliance commentary also describe staging; descriptions are not first discovered by this project.

ranking.conclusion: Substantive first-sampling discrepancy survives review for the narrow partner/non-direct-use cohort. No outdated test, infection or patient injury established.
ranking.euRequirement: Directive 2012/39 Annex (2)(c), amending 2006/17 Annex III 4.2, requires blood sampling within three months before the first partner donation outside direct use; later partner sampling may be up to 24 months apart. Base Annex III distinguishes stored/processed material and embryo cryopreservation from direct-use exemptions.
ranking.nationalVerification: Fresh live consolidated Order of 11 April 2008: header in force 26 October 2026, latest modification 11 October 2023. Annex II-5.1 permits HIV/HBV/HCV screening within six months before first relevant gamete collection. Footnote 93 defines a treatment attempt and adds no three-month override. Order of 2 June 2014 expressly substituted three months for six; Order of 5 October 2023 replaced the full annex.
ranking.significance: Concerns an infectious-screening safeguard for stored reproductive material and an apparent loss of an earlier express transposition rule during national rewriting.
contraryChecks: Direct-use partner donations and validated unstored insemination routes must not be presented as covered.
Separate third-party donor rules under R1211-25/26 were freshly read; they do not establish a general three-month partner override.
Risk assessment and retesting on newly identified contamination risk remain.
Some hospitals retain three-month protocols; current first-party provider documents also state six months. No individual treatment record reviewed.
Do not infer a doubling of infection risk from a doubling of the permitted interval.

novelty.outcome: No publication identifying the exact current EU/national mismatch located.
knownCoverage: Current three- and six-month provider instructions are public.
The 2014 and 2023 national enactments are public.
Provider instructions stating six months are not themselves an analysis of EU non-conformity.

ranking.conclusion: Verified surviving statutory under-20-MW deemed-compliance provision; practical coverage and effects require an official answer. Qualified third priority.
ranking.euRequirement: RED Article 29(1), as amended by 2023/2413, applies solid-biomass sustainability and greenhouse-gas criteria from 7.5 MW total rated thermal input for target accounting, renewable obligations and support. Article 30(6) allows simplified verification for 7.5-20 MW but still requires fulfilment of criteria.
ranking.nationalVerification: S.I.350/2022 Regulation 6(4) freshly read: under-20-MW solid biomass deemed compliant. Official amendment table freshly read, updated to 13 October 2026: no Regulation 6 or Schedule 3 amendment listed. Bounded later-enactment searches located no cure. Regulations 5(4), 6(10), 8 and 14 link support and verification to Regulation 6.
ranking.significance: Potentially leaves part of the newly covered installation band outside the substantive sustainability test, affecting the reliability of eligibility and accounting.
contraryChecks: RED Article 29(15) preserves old criteria until end-2030 for qualifying support granted before 20 November 2023, fixed long-term amount and anti-overcompensation mechanism; it applies across target accounting, obligations and support.
National Regulation 6(7)-(8) separately requires criteria for some electricity-only installations; do not generalise the concern to every plant below 20 MW.
Heat-producing installations in the band outside qualifying grandfathering provide the clearer statutory comparison.
SEAI's current verification page still points to S.I.350/2022 and RED II. Industry body IrBEA explicitly advertises RED III certification above 7.5 MW; actual practice may already be stricter.
No noncompliant fuel consignment, unlawful support payment or erroneous national count identified.
Official amendment-register cut-off is 13 October, not a certification of all enactments through 26 October.

novelty.outcome: No precise public criticism of the surviving Regulation 6(4) exemption located. New EU threshold and broad transposition delays are already known.
knownCoverage: SEAI Energy in Ireland report explains fall from 20 to 7.5 MW.
Ireland notified S.I.350/2022 under RED III on 1 July 2026; notification alone does not settle substantive conformity.

excludedFromTopThree: Hungarian bank-capital case has correct published supervisory treatment; German PV case has unresolved non-household scope; Estonian asbestos case has countervailing explicit permit rule and official guidance; Estonian lead cutoff is precise but a much narrower conditional cohort; PSD2 cases concern qualified business contracting options.
